label: SDRplay (RSP1A / RSPdx / RSPduo)
gain_description: Inverted client-side: higher slider position = more received signal. SoapySDRPlay3 reports element ranges as gain *reduction* (gRdB / LNAstate), so the raw param `gain_db` is in attenuation terms — the slider applies `displayed = max - raw` to match the universal SDR-app convention. The driver's master setGain distributes across IFGR (range 20–59) first then RFGR (0–27); peak total signal is at displayed=66 (raw=0).

rfgain_sel.label: LNA attenuation
rfgain_sel.description: Front-end LNA-state index. 0 = no attenuation (maximum gain); higher values insert attenuator stages whose dB amount depends on the frequency band — see appendix 5 of the SDRplay API spec for the exact ladder. Default 4 ≈ 37 dB attenuation at HF, which buries weak HF signals (FT8 / WSPR / SSB DX); set to 0 for HF reception. Despite the upstream SoapySDRPlay3 label of 'RF Gain Select', this is an attenuator index, not a gain knob — lower is louder.

rfnotch_ctrl.label: AM/FM broadcast notch
rfnotch_ctrl.description: RSPdx hardware notch covering AM (540–1.7 MHz) + FM (88–108 MHz) broadcast bands. Default ON to keep strong locals out when receiving away from those bands; auto-disabled when the centre is inside AM or FM.

dabnotch_ctrl.label: DAB Band III notch
dabnotch_ctrl.description: RSPdx hardware notch over DAB Band III (170–240 MHz). Default ON; auto-disabled when the centre is inside Band III.

hdr_ctrl.label: HDR mode (≤ 2 MHz only)
hdr_ctrl.description: RSPdx high-dynamic-range mode for the LF/MW bands below 2 MHz. Has no effect above 2 MHz; safe to leave default-ON.

biasT_ctrl.label: Bias-T (DC on antenna)
biasT_ctrl.description: Applies +4.7 V DC on the antenna port for active LNAs / preamps. Default OFF — turn ON only when the connected antenna explicitly needs it.

auto_settings.rationale: AM/FM broadcast notch: disable when receiving inside the AM or FM band, leave ON otherwise.
DAB Band III notch: disable inside 170–240 MHz.

notes: IF filter picked as the largest ladder entry ≤ Fs. SDRplay's own default of 200 kHz brick-walls the spectrum at ±100 kHz, and any filter wider than Fs makes the driver silently upclock Fs — so we pick from the ladder explicitly rather than leaving it to the driver. Advertised max of 10.66 MS/s fails activateStream in practice; clamped to 10 MS/s. `rfgain_sel` is exposed (with a clarifying label override) since the upstream SoapySDR label calls it a gain knob but it's actually an LNA attenuator index — leaving it default-4 caused a 37 dB drop on HF that hid weak signals.
ai_operator_notes:
SDRplay **RSPdx** — 14-bit single-tuner SDR, 1 kHz – 2 GHz, sample rates 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 MS/s. Three antenna ports — pick the one that matches the band you're tuning before debugging anything else.

### Antennas

- **Antenna A** — SMA, full 1 kHz – 2 GHz range. General-purpose for VHF / UHF with a whip / discone / dipole. Default for >30 MHz when the operator hasn't said otherwise.
- **Antenna B** — SMA, full 1 kHz – 2 GHz range, with **Bias-T (4.7 V DC)** available. Use for an active antenna / preamp that needs power; flip `biasT_ctrl=true` only then.
- **Antenna C** — **BNC high-impedance input, 1 kHz – 200 MHz, optimized for HF / MW / LW.** Best port for shortwave SWL, AM broadcast, FT8 / WSPR, NDBs, ham HF bands. For anything below 30 MHz this is usually the right choice; for VHF up to ~200 MHz it works but A/B are usually better.

If you don't know what the operator has hooked to which port, **read the `Operator-supplied radio setup` section** below. If it isn't filled in, *say so* ("I don't know what's on Antenna B — can you tell me?") rather than cycling antennas blind.

### Gain — two stages

The `--gain N` flag and the UI gain slider control the **overall** SoapySDR gain element. Under the hood it's two reduction-based stages:

1. **IFGR** (IF gain reduction, 20–59 dB) — controlled by AGC OR manual; never both. `ferrite-ctl tune --gain N` atomically sets `agc_enable=false` in the same PATCH, so manual gain just works — no separate AGC dance needed. If you *want* AGC instead, pass no `--gain` flag and leave `agc_enable=true`.
2. **LNAstate / RFGR** (`rfgain_sel`, 0–9; ~7 dB per step at HF, fewer steps at higher freq) — *always* manual, separate from `--gain`. **Lower = less attenuation = louder.** The upstream Soapy label says "RF Gain Select" but it's an attenuator index, not a gain knob.

**`rfgain_sel` is separate from `--gain`.** Default is 4 (≈ 37 dB attenuation at HF) which buries weak signals. For weak-signal HF (FT8 / WSPR / SSB DX) drop it to 0. For strong RF environments (urban FM, near an AM broadcast tower) raise it to prevent ADC overload (you'll see the waterfall ceiling at byte=255).

```
ferrite-ctl --note "max LNA gain for weak HF" param src settings='{"rfgain_sel":"0"}'
```

Gain decision tree:
- Weak HF (<30 MHz, faint carriers) → `agc_enable=false`, `rfgain_sel=0`, `--gain 50–60`.
- Strong HF / general SWL → `agc_enable=true` *or* `--gain 30` manual + `rfgain_sel=2`.
- VHF / UHF default → `agc_enable=true` or `--gain 25–35` manual.
- ADC clipping (255 ceiling) → raise `rfgain_sel` by 1–2 steps; manual gain alone may not be enough.

### Hardware notches — auto-toggled by UI

The UI auto-toggles the per-band notches based on the centre frequency (see `auto_settings` in this preset file). You don't need to manage them unless you have a specific reason:

- `rfnotch_ctrl` — AM (540 kHz – 1.7 MHz) + FM broadcast (88 – 108 MHz). Default ON for intermod rejection; auto-disabled inside those bands.
- `dabnotch_ctrl` — DAB Band III (170 – 240 MHz). Default ON; auto-disabled inside.
- `hdr_ctrl` — HDR mode for LF/MW (below 2 MHz). Default ON; no effect above 2 MHz. Safe to leave on.
- `biasT_ctrl` — DC bias on Antenna B only. Default OFF — turn ON only when the connected antenna explicitly needs it.

### Frequency-axis convention for captured FFTs

`fft_to_png.py` labels the x-axis in absolute MHz, using the `center_freq_hz` + `sample_rate_hz` stamped into the bin's sidecar JSON from PortMeta. Trust the labels — a peak at `6.500 MHz` is a 6.500 MHz carrier, not an offset.

### DC spike

Zero-IF leakage produces a constant bright vertical line at the tuned centre. Standard workaround: tune the source 50–100 kHz off-target (more for wide signals) and use the channelizer's `freq_shift_hz` to pull the actual target back to baseband for demod.
